title: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Short title, extent and commencement

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER I GENERAL
1. Short
title, extent and commencement.‑‑(1) This Ordinance may be
called the Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance, 1996.
(2) It extends to the whole of Pakistan.
(3) This section shall come into force at once and
the remaining provisions of this Ordinance shall come into force on such date
as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette,
appoint, and different dates may be so appointed for different provisions.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Definitions

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER I GENERAL
2. Definitions.‑‑In this Ordinance, unless there is
anything repugnant in the subject or
context,‑‑
(a) "Authority" means the National Electric
Power Regulatory Authority established under section 3;
(b) "bulk‑power consumer" means a
consumer who purchases or receives electric power in an amount of one magawatt
or more or in such amount and voltage level and with such other characteristics
as the Authority may determine;
(c) "Chairman" means
the Chairman of the Authority;
(d) "consumer" means
a person or his successor‑in‑interest who purchases or receives
electric power for consumption and not for delivery or sale to others,
including a person that owns or occupies a premises where electric power is
supplied;
(e) "distribution"
means the ownership, operation, management or control of distribution
facilities for the movement, delivery or sale of electric power to consumers:
Provided that the ownership,
operation, management and control of distribution facilities located on private
property and used solely to move or deliver electric power to the person owing,
operating, managing and controlling those facilities
or to tenants thereof shall not constitute distribution;
(f) "distribution company" means a person,
firm, association of persons, company or undertaking engaged in distribution of
electric power;
(g) "distribution facilities" means
electrical facilities operating at distribution voltage and used for the
movement or delivery of electric power;
(h) "distribution
voltage" means any voltage below minimum transmission voltage;
(i) "electric power" means electrical
energy or the capacity for the production of electrical power;
(j) "electric power services" means the
transmission, generation or distribution of electric power;
(k) "generation" means the ownership,
operation, management or control of generation facilities for sale to
distribution companies or to consumers .end not solely for consumption by the
person owning, operating, managing, and controlling those facilities;
(1) "generation, company" means a person,
firm, association of persons, company or undertaking engaged in generation of
electric power;
(m) "generation facility" means the electrical
facility used for the production of electric power;
(n) "inter‑connection
service" means the safe and reliable connection of one company's
electrical facilities to another company's. electrical facilities;
(o) "Karachi Electricity
Supply Corporation or KESC" means the Karachi Electric Supply Corporation,
Karachi;
(p) "licence" means a licence issued for
generation, transmission or distribution under this Ordinance;
(q) "licensee" means
a holder of a licence;
(r) "member" means
the member of the Authority;
(s) "minimum transmission voltage" means
sixty‑six kilovolts or such other voltage that the Authority may
determine to be the minimum voltage at which electrical facilities are operated
when used to deliver electric power in bulk;
(t) "national grid company" means the
person, firm, association of persons, company or undertaking engaged in the
transmission of electric power and granted a licence under this Ordinance for
the said purpose;
(u) "prescribed"
means prescribed by rules made under this Ordinance;
(v) "public sector project" means
generation, transmission or distribution facilities constructed, owned, managed
or controlled by the Federal Government, a Provincial Government, local
authority or any corporation owned or controlled by any such Government or
authority;
(w) "regulations"
means regulations made under this Ordinance;
(x) "transmission" means the ownership,
operation, management or control of transmission facilities for whatever
purpose;
(y) "transmission facilities" means electrical
facilities, including electrical circuits, transformers and substations
operating at or above minimum transmission voltage:

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Establishment of the authority

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF AUTHORITY
3. Establishment
of the Authority.‑‑(1) As soon as may be, after the
commencement of this Ordinance, the Federal Government shall establish a
National Electric Power Regulatory Authority consisting of a Chairman to be
appointed by the Federal Government and four members one from each Province to
be appointed by the Federal Government in consultation with the respective
Provincial Governments:
Provided that no person shall be appointed as a
Chairman or member who has attained the age of seventy years.
(2) There shall be a Vice‑Chairman of the
Authority, appointed from amongst the members for a period of one year, by
rotation, in the following order, namely:‑‑
(i) the member representing Province of Balochistan;
(ii) the member representing
Province of North‑West Frontier;
(iii) the member representing
Province of the Punjab; and
(iv) the member representing
Province of Sindh.
(3) The Chairman shall be an
eminent person of known integrity and competence with at least twenty years of
relevant experience in Government law, I)r electric utility business.
(4) Every member shall be a
person of known integrity and competence with
at least fifteen years of related experience in Government, law, business,
engineering, finance, accounting, economics or a related discipline.
(5) The Chairman and members
shall, unless resigned or removed earlier as hereinafter provided, hold office
for a term of four years and shall be eligible for re‑appointment for a
similar term.
(6) In the case of death,
resignation or removal of a Chairman or a member, another Chairman or, as the
case may be, a member may be appointed in his place for the un-expired term of
such Chairman or member.
(7) No act or proceeding of the
Authority shall be invalid by reason only of existence of a vacancy in, or
defect in, the constitution of the Authority.
(8) The principal office of the
Authority shall be in Islamabad and it may set up offices at such place or
places as it may deem appropriate.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Resignation and removal of chairman, etc.

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF AUTHORITY
4. Resignation and removal of Chairman, etc.‑‑(1) The
Chairman or a member may, by writing under his hand, resign from his office.
(2) The Federal Government may,
in its discretion and in the public interest, terminate the appointment of the
Chairman or any Member at any time before the expiry of the period of such
appointment.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Meeting of the authority etc.

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF AUTHORITY
5. Meetings of the Authority, etc.‑‑(1) The meetings of
the Authority shall be presided over by the Chairman or, in his absence, by the
Vice -Chairman.
(2) Three members shall
constitute a quorum for meetings of the Authority requiring a decision by the
Authority:
Provided that each member of
the Authority must have notice of the time and place that a matter requiring a
decision by the Authority shall be taken in such meeting.
(3) The decision of the
Authority shall be taken with the concurrence of the majority of its members,
including the Chairman, and in case of tie, the Chairman shall have a casting
vote.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Powers and functions of the authority

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF AUTHORITY
6. Powers and functions of the Authority.‑‑(1) The
Authority shall be responsible for regulating the grant of licences for generation,
transmission and distribution of electric power.
(2) In particular and without prejudice to the
generality of the foregoing power, the Authority shall‑‑
(a) grant licences for generation, transmission and
distribution of electric power;
(b) approve tariff, rates, charges and other terms
and conditions for supply of electric power services by the generation,
transmission and distribution companies;
(c) prescribe procedures and standards for investment
programmes by generation, transmission and distribution companies;
(d) review organizational affairs of the transmission
and distribution companies to avoid any adverse effect on the operation of the
electric power and for continuance and efficient supply of such power;
(e) develop and enforce performance standards for
generation, transmission and distribution companies;
(f) encourage uniform industry
standards and code of conduct for generation, transmission and distribution
companies;
(g) establish a uniform system of accounts by
generation, transmission and distribution companies;
(h) tender advice to the public
sector projects;
(i) submit reports to the
Federal Government in respect of activities of the generation, transmission and
distribution companies;
(j) levy fees, with the
approval of the Federal Government, for grant of licences and renewal thereof;
(k) prescribe fines for
contravention of the provisions of this Ordinance; and
(1) perform any other function
which is incidental or consequential to any of the aforesaid functions.
(3) In performing its functions
under this Ordinance, the Authority shall, as far as practicable, protect the
interests of consumers and companies providing electric power services in
accordance with the guidelines laid down by Federal Government

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Remuneration, etc., of chairman and members

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF AUTHORITY
7. Remuneration,
etc., of Chairman and members.‑‑(1) The Chairman and members
shall be paid such emoluments as may be determined by the oral Government but
such emoluments shall not be less than the salary and perquisites admissible to
the Judge of the High Court and shall not be varied to their disadvantage
during their term of office:
Provided that the Chairman and
members shall not, during their term office, engage themselves in any other
service, business, vocation or employment;
Provided further that for two
years after the conclusion of their terms office the Chairman and, as the case
may be, a member shall not enter into the employment of, or accept any advisory
or consultancy relationship with, any person engaged in the generation,
transmission or distribution of electric power in Pakistan or any related
undertaking.
(2 )During their term of office
the spouses and children of the Chairman and members shall not have any direct
or indirect financial interest, or have connection with any company connected
with the generation, transmission or distribution of electric power nor such
spouses and children shall enter into employment of, or accept any advisory or
consultancy relationship with, such companies.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996

Chairman, etc., to the public servant

PAKISTAN

8. Chairman, etc., to be public servant.‑‑The Chairman,
members of staff, experts, consultants, advisors and other employees of the
Authority, when acting or purporting to act in pursuance of any of the
provisions of this Ordinance, shall be deemed to public servants within the
meaning of section 21 of the Pakistan Penal Code; 1860 (Act XLV of 1860).

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Delegation

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF AUTHORITY
11. Delegation.‑‑The
Authority may delegate to the Chairman, a member or any of its officer or
special Tribunal all or any of its powers, functions or duties under this
Ordinance, except‑
(a) the power to grant, reject,
condition, amend, vary or revoke licences;
(b) the power to approve,
disapprove or modify tariffs;
(c) the power to approve,
disapprove or modify an Investment Programme and Power Acquisition Programme;
(d) power to make or .repeal
rules and regulations made under this Ordinance; and
(e) power to make orders on an
application for review of its orders.

Funds

12. Funds.‑‑(1) The operations of the
Authority shall be funded from‑‑
(a) the grants from the Federal Government, including
an initial grant of one hundred million rupees; and
(b) fees and fines collected by it for processing
various applications under this Ordinance and other fees payable by the
licensees.
(2) The funds of the Authority shall be administered
through accounts to be maintained with the banks as may be approved by the
Federal Government.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Generation licence

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
15 Generation Licence.‑(1) No person, firm, association of
persons, coin any or undertaking shall construct, own or operate a generation
facility unless he or it holds a
generation licence under this Ordinance.
(2) An application for grant of a licence for
generation facility shall specify ‑
(i) the type of facility for
which the licence is applied;
(ii) the location of the generation facility; and
(iii) the expected life of the
generation facility
(3) The Authority may, after
such enquiry as it may deem appropriate and subject to the conditions specified
in this Ordinance as it may impose, grant licence authorising the licensee to
construct, own or operate connected generation facility:
Provided that such licence
shall be granted for one generation facility or group of generation facility or
group of generation facilities located at the same site.
(4) For generation facility
connecting directly or indirectly to the national grid company, the licensee of
the generation facility shall, subject to the compensation fixed by the
Authority for voltage support and uneconomic dispatch directed by the National
Grid Company, make available to the national grid company safe, reliable non‑discriminatory
dispatch and operation of the national transmission g facilities.

16. Transmission licence.‑‑(1) No person, firm, association
of persons, company or undertaking shall, except in the territory served by the
Karachi Electric Supply Corporation, engage in the transmission of electric
power unless such person holds a
transmission licence issued by the Authority under this Ordinance
(2) An application for licence
for transmission of electric power shall specify‑‑
(i) the type of service for
which the licence is being sought; and
(ii) the territory with
location maps and plans to which the electric power shall be transmitted.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
National grid company

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
17. National
Grid Company.‑‑(1) The Authority may, after such enquiry as it
may deem appropriate and subject to the conditions specified in this Ordinance
and as it may impose, grant a licence authorising the licensee, hereinafter to
be called the National Grid Company, to engage in the transmission of electric
power for delivery to distribution companies and bulk power consumers:
Provided that only one such licence shall be granted
at any one time.
(2) The licence referred to in
subsection (1) shall have, except in the territory served by Karachi Electric
Supply Corporation, exclusive right to provide transmission service in the
territory specified in such licence.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Responsibilities of national grid company

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
18. Responsibilities
of National Grid Company.‑‑(1) The National Grid Company shall
be responsible to operate and provide safe, reliable transmission and inter‑connection
services on a non‑discriminatory basis, including a bulk power consumer
who proposes to become directly connected to its facilities.
(2) Without prejudice to the foregoing
responsibilities, the National Grid Company‑‑
(a) shall make available to the
general public the tariffs of electric power transmission specifying the
Authority's approved rates, charges and other terms and conditions of
transmission and inter‑connection services;
(b) shall not levy any rate of charge or impose any
condition for supply of electric power which have not been approved by the
Authority as a tariff;
(c) shall not, including the Karachi Electricity
Supply Corporation (KESC) and Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority
(WAPDA), till their electric systems are fully desegregated, cause a division
or any of associated undertaking to engage in generation and distribution; and
(d) shall develop, maintain and publicly make
available, with the prior approval of the Authority, an investment performance for
satisfying its service, obligation and acquiring and selling its assets.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Special purpose transmission licence

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
19. Special
purpose transmission licence.‑‑Notwithstanding anything
contained in section 17, the Authority may, in public interest, grant a licence
authorising the licensee to engage in the construction, ownership and operation
specified transmission facilities on the conditions that the licensee shall ---‑‑
(a) provide transmission and inter‑connection
services to the National Grid Company and to others, wherever necessary, at
such rates, charges and terms and conditions as may be approved by the
Authority;
(b) purchase inter‑connection service from the
National Grid Company as may be necessary and to connect its facilities to the
national transmission grid at the rates, charges and terms and conditions
approved by the Authority .
(c) make its transmission
facilities available for operation by the National Grid Company consistent with
applicable instructions established by such comp" ,
(d) follow the performance
standards laid down by the Authority for transmission of electric power,
including safety, health and environmental protection instructions issued by
the Authority or any Governmental agency;
(e) make public the tariff
specifying the Authority's rates, charges and other terms and conditions of
service for transmission and inter‑connection Services; and
(f) maintain accounts in
accordance with the manner and procedure specified by the Authority.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Distribution licences

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
20. Distribution
licences.‑‑(1) No person, firm, association of persons, company
or undertaking shall, unless holds a licence issued by the Authority under this
Ordinance and subject to such conditions as may be imposed by the ,Authority,
engage in distribution of electric power.
(2) An application for licence
for distribution of electric power shall
specify---
(i) the type of service for
which the licence is being sought;
(ii) the territory in which the
electric power shall be distributed; and
(iii) source and scope of
electric power and rates paid by it.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Duties and responsibilities of the distribution licensees

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
21. Duties and
responsibilities of the distribution licensees.‑‑(1) The
Authority may after such enquiry as it may deem appropriate and subject to such
conditions specified in this Ordinance and as it may impose, grant a licence
distribution of electric power.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in subsection
(1), the licensee shall‑‑
(a) possess the exclusive right to provide
distribution service and to make sales of electric power to consumers in the
territory specified in the licence:
Provided that a generation company may make sales of
electric power to bulk‑power consumers within such territory 9s the
Authority may, subject to subsection (3) for a period of fifteen years, allow;
and
(b) responsible to provide distribution service and
make sales of electric power within its territory on a non‑discriminatory
basis to all the consumers who meet eligibility criteria laid down by the
Authority:
Provided that‑‑
(i) the licensee may not make sale of electric power
to a bulk‑power consumer who has contracted for electric power supply
from another supplier; and
(ii) the licensee may disconnect the provision of
electric power to a consumer for default in payment of power charges or to a
consumer who is involved in theft of electric power;
(c) publicly make available tariff specifying the
Authority's approved rates, charges and other terms and conditions for
distribution services and power sales to consumers;
(d) establish, within three months of the issue of
licence for distribution of electric power and make available to public
instructions specifying‑‑
(i) procedures for obtaining
service; and
(ii) manner and procedure for metering, billing and
collection of the licensee's approved charges and disconnection in case of non‑payment
of charges, electric power theft and use of energy for purposes other than for
which it was supplied and procedures for re‑connection and recovery of
arrears and other charges;
(e) make its transmission facilities available for
operation by the National Grid Company consistent with applicable instructions
established by such Company;
(f) follow the performance standards laid down by the
Authority for transmission of electric power, including safety, health and
environmental protection instructions issued by the Authority or any
Governmental agency; and
(g) maintain accounts in accordance with the manner
and procedure laid down by the Authority.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Sale to bulk-power consumers

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
22. Sale to
bulk‑power consumers.‑‑(1) 'Notwithstanding anything
contained in section 20‑.
(a) for fifteen years from the commencement of this
Ordinance, the Authority may permit a generation company or a distribution
company to sell electric power to bulk‑power consumers located in the
service territory of another distribution company:
Provided that such permission
shall be granted‑‑
(i) on case to case basis on an application made in
writing by a generation company or distribution company; and
(ii) if the bulk‑power consumer has not
defaulted in previous charges of electric power to any other distribution
company.
(2) Where a bulk‑power consumer intends to
cease purchases from a company, it shall convey its intentions by notice in
writing three years before such cessions;
Provided that such consumer shall continue to make
payments to the distribution company equal to the amount of cross‑subsidy
for uneconomic service for which it would otherwise have provided through sale
of electric power;

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996

Sale of electric power to the other distribution companies

ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996

23. Sale of electric power to other distribution companies.‑‑A
distribution company may sell electric power to other distribution companies
and distribute electric power sold by generation companies to other
distribution companies m the bulk‑power consumers within its service
territory subject to the provision, of section 22 in accordance with the rates,
charges and other terms and condition, of service for such sales as approved by
the Authority.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996

Licensees to be companies

ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996

24. Licensees to be companies.‑‑As far as
practicable every licensee for generation, transmission or distribution
facilities shall, except the Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority or
any concern specially exempted, get itself registered as a company in
accordance with the provisions of the Companies Ordinance, 1984 (XLVII of

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Karachi electric supply company

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
25. Karachi
Electric Supply Company.‑‑(1) Notwithstanding anything
contained hereinbefore and subject to provisions of this section, the Authority
may grant a licence for generation, transmission and distribution of electric
Power to a licensee for the territory served by the Karachi Electric Supply
Corporation (KESC);.
Provided that only one such
licence shall be issued at any time;
Provided further that for first six months from the
commencement of this Ordinance, the KESC shall be the exclusive licensee for
such territory during which period KESC shall apply for a licence for
generation, transmission and distribution of electric power.
(2) Where a licence under this section is granted to
the KESC, the conditions applicable to a licensee for generation, transmission
and distribution of electric power shall equally be applicable to KESC:
Provided that in case of any condition applicable to
the KESC before the commencement of this Ordinance which may be inconsistent
with the condition of a licence issued under this Ordinance, the condition
applicable to KESC before such commencement shall remain effective in force:
Provided further that where the licence of the KESC
is revoked and in its place a licence for generation, transmission or
distribution of electric power is granted to another company or the KESC
transfers its shares to another company, such company shall be bound by all the
conditions applicable under this Ordinance.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:

26. Companies
not to function within the territory served by KESC and WAPDA.‑‑Notwithstanding
anything contained in this Ordinance, no company or undertaking shall be
allowed generation or transmission of electric power unless the KESC or WAPDA
is fully desegregated.

ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
28. Assignment,
etc.‑‑(1) A generation company issued a licence Under this
Ordinance may, subject to thirty days prior notice to the Authority, assign or
transfer its licence to another company.
(2) A licensee for generation or transmission of
electric power shall not, without the prior approval of the Authority,
surrender, assign or transfer its licence to any person, firm, association of
persons, ' company or undertaking.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Penalties

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
29. Penalties.‑‑Notwithstanding any other
penalty of suspension or revocation of a licence for contravention of a licence
granted under this Ordinance, the Authority may impose a fine which may extend
to three hundred thousand rupees for each violation for each day and where any
contravention continues, may impose a higher penalty as may be prescribed:
Provided that the licensee shall, before imposition
of any penalty under this section, be given a notice to show cause and provided
with an opportunity of being heard.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Suspension and revocation

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
30 Suspension and revocation.‑‑(1) The Authority may
suspend or revoke any licence issued under this Ordinance for consistent
failure of the licensee to comply with the conditions of the licence:
Provided that before taking
action under this section, the Authority shall issue a notice to the licensee
to show cause and may provide an opportunity to rectify the omission subject to
such conditions as the Authority may specify.
(2) Where the Authority revokes
a licence, it may undertake all or any of the following actions for continuance
of the facilities covered under the licence, namely:‑‑
(a) permit the licensee to
continue operating such facilities under such terms and conditions as the
Authority shall specify;
(b) contract with another
company to immediately take over the operation. or
(c) appoint an administrator to take over the
operation of the licensed facilities.
(3) The action specified in subsection (2) may
continue till a successor licensee takes over the charge of the facilities on
such terms and conditions as the Authority may determine, including payment of
compensation for the plants, machinery, and other equipments installed at a facility
of the licensee whose licence was revoked.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Pakistan water and power development authority to be a licensee

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
31. Pakistan
Water and Power Development Authority to be a licensee.‑‑‑
Notwithstanding anything contained hereinbefore, the Pakistan Water and Power
Development Authority (WAPDA) shall, from the commencement of this Ordinance,.
be a licensee under the provisions of this Ordinance and shall be subject to
the terms and conditions applicable to other licensees under this Ordinance:
Provided that within six months from the commencement
of this Ordinance, the WAPDA shall apply for licences for the generation,
transmission and distribution of electric power:
Provided further that till the WAPDA facilities are
finally desegregated, it may continue to apply its own rates and charges and
terms and conditions for generation, transmission and distribution in
accordance with the provisions applicable before the commencement of this
Ordinance.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Tariffs

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
32 Tariffs.‑‑(1)
The Authority shall, within one year from the commencement of this
Ordinance, determine procedures and standards for approval, modification or
revision of rates, charges and terms and conditions for transmission, inter‑connection
services, distribution services and power sales' to consumers by the licensees.
(2) The Authority while determining the standards
referred to in subsection (1) shall‑‑
(a) protect consumers against
monopolistic prices;
(b) permit licensees to recover their costs of
providing electric power service so as to attract financing for capital
improvements and new construction and to meet the requirements of companies
approved investment and power acquisition programmes approved by the Authority;
(c) encourage efficiency in
licensee's operations and quality of service;
(d) encourage economic
efficiency in the electric power industry;
(e) permit distribution companies to recover all
costs incurred by those companies under power purchase contract;
(f) keep in view the adjustment of the subsidies made
by the Federal Government and manner and extent of its recovery; and
(g) determine tariffs so as to
minimize the economic distortions.
(3) The procedures established
under subsection (1) by the Authority shall include‑‑
(a) time frames for tariff
applications and decisions by the Authority;
(b) opportunity for customers and other interested
parties to participate meaningfully in the tariff approval process; and .
(c) refund protection for
customers while tariff decisions are pending.
(4) The rates and charges for sale of electric power
to bulk‑power consumers shall be regulated by the Authority subject to
the prior approval of the Federal Government.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Investment and power acquisition programs

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
33. Investment
and power acquisition programmes.‑‑(1) The Authority shall,
within eighteen months from the commencement of this Ordinance, establish
procedures and standards for the Authority's prior approval of the, National
Grid Company's investment programmes and distribution companies investment and
power acquisition programmes.
(2) Any procedures established by the Authority under
this section shall advance the goal of minimizing regulatory oversight of
contracts entered into‑by the National Grid Company and distribution
companies.
(3) Any Investment Programme or Investment and Power
Acquisition Programme approved by the Authority under this section shall take
into account national energy plans issued by the Federal Government.
(4) Upon the Authority's
approval of an Investment and Power Acquisition Programme, the Authority shall,
subject to such terms and conditions including rates and charges of electric
power, permit the distribution company to enter into long term contracts for
power purchases.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Organizational matters

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
34. Organizational
matters.‑‑Subject to the procedures established by the
Authority under this Ordinance, the Authority tray, in the public interest,
with or without modifications, approve the following activities by licensee of
transmission and distribution company, namely:‑‑
(a) the undertaking of a merger or a major
acquisition or sale of facilities;
(b) the expansion of the
licensee's business activities; and
(c) the undertaking of a re‑organization
of the licensee's business structure.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Performance standards

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
35. Performance standards.‑‑The Authority shall prescribe
performance standards for generation, transmission and distribution companies
to encourage safe, efficient and reliable service, including standards for‑‑--
(i) service characteristics such as voltage and
stability;
(ii) scheduled and unscheduled outages;
(iii) reserve margins;
(iv) time required to connect new customers
Provided that the distribution companies shall be
required to establish new connections within fourteen days of the receipt of a
request for service unless the Authority, in special circumstances, extend such
period for another fourteen days; and
(v) number and duration of load
shedding period

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Industry standards and codes of conduct

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
36. Industry standards and codes of conduct.‑‑The Authority
shall encourage the development of industry performance standards and uniform
codes of conduct so as to provide‑‑
(a) planning criteria for
safety, reliability and cost effectiveness of the generation, transmission and
distribution facilities;
(b) construction practices and
standards of such facilities;
(c) operating standards and
procedures;
(d) maintenance schedules;
(e) maintenance of adequate
spinning reserves and plans to satisfy demand
(f) equipment specification and standardization; and
(g) load shedding and
restoration procedures.

Uniform system of accounts

CHAPTER III
LICENCES
37. Uniform system of accounts.‑‑The Authority shall
prescribe a uniform system of accounts which shall be followed by the licensee
of generation, transmission and distribution facilities within such period as
may be prescribed.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Review of public sector projects

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER III
LICENCES
38. Review of
public sector projects.‑‑(1) For any public sector project,
other than transmission projects undertaken by WAPDA, the advice of the Authority
shall be sought by the agency planning to, undertaking such projects.
(2) The Authority shall, before granting approval to
any project, consider‑‑
(a) whether the proposed
project was needed to prevent power shortages or to reach unserved customers; ,
(b) whether the private sector is willing and able to
undertake the proposed project or other projects that would serve the intended
purpose of the proposed project; and
(c) what action the agency undertaking the proposed
project could take to encourage private investment in that project.
(d) the agency undertaking public sector project
shall consider the Authority's recommendations and, for any public sector
project that is undertaken, shall seek to involve the private sector in the
construction, operation and maintenance of the project.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Provincial offices of inspection

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
39 Provincial offices of inspection.‑‑Each Provincial
Government shall‑‑
(a) establish offices of
inspection that shall be empowered to‑‑
(i) enforce compliance with distribution companies'
instructions respecting metering, billing, electricity consumption charges and
decision of cases of theft of energy; and
(ii) make determination in respect of disputes
over-metering, billing and collection of tariff;
(b) establish procedures whereby distribution
companies and consumers may prosecute, before the office of inspection,
violations of the companies' instructions in respect of metering, billing and
collection of tariff and other connected matters; and
(c) enforce penalties for contravention of the
determination made by the Provincial Government under this section.
Explanation.‑‑The
Electric Inspector appointed by the Provincial Governments under section 36
of the Electricity Act, 1910 (IX of 1910), may, in addition to their duties
under the said Ordinance, be assigned the duties of the offices of inspection
under this Ordinance.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Decision of the authority

PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996

40. Decision
of the Authority.‑‑All orders, determinations and decisions of
the Authority shall be taken in writing and shall identify the determination of
the Chairman and each member.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Complaints

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
41. Complaints.‑‑(1)
Any interested person, including a Provincial Government, may file a
written complaint with the Authority against a licensee for contravention of
any provision of this Ordinance or any order, regulation, licence or
instruction made or issued thereunder.
(2) The Authority shall, on receipt of a complaint,
provide the opportunity of show cause to the licensee or any other person
against whom such complaint has been made before taking any action thereon.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Review and appeals

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
42. Review and
Appeals.‑‑(1) In the case, any person aggrieved by an order
made by the Authority made under this Ordinance may, within thirty days of that
order, prefer an application to the Authority for review thereof if the amount
in dispute is three thousand rupees or less.
(2) Any person, including a Provincial Government,
aggrieved of an order of the Authority involving an amount over three thousand
rupees or of an order of Tribunal passed under section 10 may, within thirty
days of that order, prefer an appeal against such order to the High Court in
accordance with the rules applicable for filing of first appeal in the said
Court.
(3) Subject to the provisions of subsections (1) and
(2) no order, determination or decision of the Authority shall be called into
question before any Court or Tribunal.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Enforcement of order of the authority

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
43. Enforcement
of orders of the Authority.‑‑The
Authority's determinations under this Ordinance shall be deemed to be a
decree of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure Act, 1908 (V of
1908).

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Reports of the authority

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
44. Reports of
the Authority.‑‑(1) The Authority shall submit to the Federal
Government at the end of every financial year, but before the last day of
September of that year‑‑
(a) a report on the conduct of its affairs for that
year, including anticipated developments for the following year; and
(b) report. on the state of the electric power
industries .in the country identifying the ownership, operation, management and
control of electric power facilities, amount of transmission and generation
capacity, present and future demand of electricity, cost of electric power
services and other matters relating to electric power industry .
(2) Every licensee shall submit to the Authority
reports, statements and other information as the Authority may require in
respect of safe, reliable and economic dispatch and operation of the national
transmission grid and connected facilities maintained by them.
(3) The Provincial Governments may, upon request by
the Authority submit to the Authority‑‑
(a) a copy of any document in the charge of the
Provincial Government relating to Provincial Officers of inspection; and
(b) other reports. statements and information as the
Authority determines to be necessary or appropriate for the Authority's
periodic assessment of the effectiveness of inspection made by Provincial
Officers of inspection.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Inspection by public

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
45. Inspection
by public.‑‑(1) The Authority shall maintain public files that
shall be kept open in convenient form for public inspection and examination
during reasonable business hours.
(2) Subject to procedures and
standards for confidentiality, the Authority's public files shall include all
relevant documents to be maintained and indexed as the Authority deems fit.
(3) The Provincial Governments
shall keep open in convenient form for public inspection and examination during
reasonable business hours all complaints, responses and decisions relating to
the Provincial Inspection Offices.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Hydel resources

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
46. Hydel resources.‑‑The
provision of this Ordinance shall only apply to the regulation of hydel
resources established in the public sector projects or owned, maintained and
controlled by WAPDA at the commencement of this Ordinance.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Relationship to other laws

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
47. Relationship to other laws.‑‑The provisions of this
Ordinance, rules and regulations made and licences issued thereunder shall have
effect notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law,
rule or regulation, for the time being in force and any such law, rules or
regulations shall, to the extent of any inconsistency, cease to have any effect
from the date this Ordinance comes into force and the Authority shall subject
to the provision of this Ordinance, be exclusively empowered to determine
rates, charges and other terms and conditions for electric power services:
Provided that nothing in this
Ordinance shall affect the jurisdiction,
powers or determinations of the Corporate Law
Authority or the Monopolies Control Board.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Rules

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
48. Rules.‑‑(1) The
Authority may, with the prior approval of the Federal Government, make rules to
carry out the purposes of this Ordinance.
(2) Without prejudice to the
generality of the foregoing powers, such rules may provide for‑‑
(a) procedure for seeking
nominations of members from the Provincial Governments;
(b) the form and manner of
application to be made for a licence for generation, transmission or
distribution facilities;
(c) the fees and documents to
be accompanied with the applications for licences;
(d) determination of rates,
charges and other terms and conditions of licences;
(e) procedure for recovery of
fines as arrears of land revenue;
(f) publication of rates and
charges of electricity consumption, procedure for metering, billing and
collection of electric power charges by the licensees;
(g) procedure for resolving
disputes amongst the licensees and consumers and the licensees;
(h) procedure for submission of
various reports to the Federal Government and the manner of preparation of such
reports;
(i) procedure for inquiry and investigation into the
affairs of an applicant for a licence and for any contravention of any provision
of this Ordinance;
(j) the manner and procedure of
show‑cause notices;
(k) safe, effective and
environmental free supply of electric power;
(1) performance and industrial standards for supply
of electric power; and
(m) standards for Investment Programmes for
transmission companies and Investment and Power Acquisition Programmes for
distribution companies.

sections.shortTitle: Pakistan Electric Power Regulatory Authority Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Regulations

ORDINANCE C OF 1996
PAKISTAN
ELECTRIC POWER REGULATORY AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1996
CHAPTER IV ADMINISTRATION
49. Regulations.‑‑(1)
The Authority may make regulations not inconsistent with the provisions of
this Ordinance or the rules made thereunder.
(2) Without prejudice to the foregoing powers; such
regulations may provide for appointment of its officers, members of staff and
such other persons and terms and conditions of their service.
